mistakes.title: Missing decoupling capacitor
mistakes.explanation: U1 has a power pin on net '+1V2', but no bypass/decoupling capacitor connects that net to a recognized ground return. Without local decoupling, supply transients from switching current can couple into the IC and cause glitches, resets, or radiated noise.
mistakes.fix_suggestion: Add a decoupling capacitor (typically 100nF, or per the datasheet) from +1V2 to the nearest ground return, placed within a few mm of U1's power pin.

mistakes.title: Power trace too narrow
mistakes.explanation: Power trace on +1V2 is only 0.20mm wide. Narrow power traces cause voltage drop and can overheat under load. For 1A at 1oz copper, traces should be at least 0.5mm wide.
mistakes.fix_suggestion: Increase trace width on +1V2 to at least 0.3mm, or use a copper pour for power distribution. Consider the expected current draw.

mistakes.title: Acute angle in trace (acid trap)
mistakes.explanation: Trace on DQ2 (F.Cu) has a 90° angle. Angles less than 90° can trap etchant during PCB manufacturing, causing over-etching at the vertex. This can weaken the trace and cause reliability issues.
mistakes.fix_suggestion: Reroute the trace to use 45° or 90° angles instead. If the acute angle is unavoidable, add a teardrop at the junction to eliminate the sharp corner.
